current_disclosures.summary: NAND products are non-volatile, re-writeable storage devices used in SSDs, managed NAND, and low-density applications across data center, PC, consumer, and automotive markets. In 2024, volume production began for Micron G9 NAND, the industry's ninth-generation 3D NAND node, and the majority of 2025 NAND bit production was on leading-edge G8 and G9 nodes. The NAND Flash offering includes triple-level cell (TLC) and quad-level cell (QLC) technologies with varying density, performance, and endurance characteristics.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded Processor and GPU Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers embedded CPUs, APUs, and GPUs, including EPYC Embedded, Ryzen Embedded V/R-Series, and Radeon Embedded products, designed for high-performance compute, networking, storage, and graphics in enterprise and automotive markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe specific product portfolios targeting overlapping end markets, particularly automotive and storage. Micron discloses that NAND products are used in SSDs for data centers and automotive markets, while AMD details its embedded CPUs, APUs, and GPUs which are designed to support high-performance storage requirements for enterprise/cloud infrastructure as well as automotive infotainment systems. The similarity lies in the shared focus on storage and automotive applications, while the difference is that Micron provides the underlying NAND storage media itself, whereas AMD provides the processing and control logic (CPUs/GPUs) enabling those storage and automotive functions.

sentences.text: NAND is used in SSDs for the data center, client PC, consumer, and automotive markets and in removable storage markets.
Low-density NAND is ideal for applications like automotive, surveillance, machine-to-machine, automation, printer, and home networking.

Our embedded processors and GPUs are designed to support high performance compute, high-bandwidth network connectivity and security, high-performance storage requirements for enterprise and cloud infrastructure, 3D graphics performance and 4K multimedia requirements of automotive infotainment systems.

comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom develops complex digital/mixed signal CMOS and analog III-V semiconductor devices, offering thousands of products for markets including AI networking, data centers, telecommunications, and factory automation.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify data center and storage systems as key end markets for their semiconductor products. Broadcom states its products are used in data center servers and storage systems, similar to Micron's NAND products which are used in SSDs for data centers. The difference is in the product nature: Broadcom provides the networking, connectivity, and complex digital/mixed-signal devices that facilitate data center operations, while Micron provides the high-capacity non-volatile semiconductor storage media.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's key strategy involves advancing its accelerated computing platform to solve complex problems with higher performance and lower power consumption than alternatives. This full-stack innovation approach leverages GPUs, CUDA, and networking technologies to serve diverse end markets including Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies target the Data Center and Automotive markets with their core technologies. Micron lists data center and automotive as primary markets for its NAND and managed NAND products. NVIDIA lists Data Center and Automotive as two of its four large target markets, leveraging its accelerated computing platform. The difference is functional: Micron provides the storage layer (NAND) within these systems, while NVIDIA provides the compute acceleration (GPUs) and networking technologies that process data within those same environments.
